ranked_facts.why: The presence of 35% blasts in the leukocyte count is more consistent with a myeloid neoplasm, such as acute myelogenous leukemia, than with a lymphoid neoplasm, as the blast percentage is a key diagnostic criterion for myeloid malignancies.

The full spectrum of maturing myeloid cells on smear is more typical of myeloid neoplasms, which often exhibit a wide range of myeloid cell maturation, whereas lymphoid neoplasms tend to have a more uniform cellular appearance.
